items.body: Murray (hamstring), who is dealing with a sore hamstring, is undergoing a full evaluation to determine the extent of the issue, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports. When asked whether or not Murray's hamstring soreness will affect his availability for next Monday night's game against the Bills, coach Kevin O'Connell told Lewis, "I don't think we're there yet." Added context regarding the QB's Week 9 availability is in line to arrive no later than Thursday's practice report, but if Murray is unable suit up versus Buffalo, Carson Wentz is next in line for Minnesota's signal-caller reps.

items.head: Navigates hamstring issue in loss
items.body: Murray completed 17 of 29 passes for 210 yards with two touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 35 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass and dealt with hamstring tightness during the game, per Alec Lewis of The Athletic. Murray was serviceable in the divisional clash in enemy territory, tossing multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season. He connected with Justin Jefferson (one yard) and T.J. Hockenson (eight yards) for his pair of scoring strikes, the former featuring a magnificent one-handed grab on the part of the star wide receiver. Murray's hamstring issue will be something to monitor ahead of a Week 9 home showdown against Josh Allen and the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9, with updates on that front expected in the coming days.

items.head: Saleh calls Ridley's incident at Nashville airport 'minor miscommunication'
items.body: Titans wide receiver Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport over the weekend that coach Robert Saleh called a "minor miscommunication" when asked about it after the team returned from the bye on Monday.

items.head: Involved in airport 'incident' over weekend
items.body: Titans head coach Robert Saleh confirmed Monday that Ridley was involved in an "unfortunate" interaction over the weekend at Nashville International Airport that is now in the hands of law enforcement, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports. Though neither the Titans nor the police have publicly shared details pertaining to the incident, Saleh described it as a "very minor miscommunication." Saleh didn't indicate that Ridley's availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars is in any jeopardy following the incident, though the 31-year-old wideout could be a candidate to get dealt elsewhere ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Ridley has been limited to six receptions for 91 yards on 13 targets through seven appearances and doesn't look to be a major part of the 1-7 Titans' immediate or long-term plans.

items.head: Titans WR Calvin Ridley involved in incident at Nashville airport
items.body: Titans WR Calvin Ridley was involved in an incident at Nashville International Airport over the weekend, details of which have not been released.

items.head: Good to go vs. Cincinnati
items.body: Ridley (hip) is active for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports. Ridley has been officially cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a hip injury. The veteran wide receiver has only five catches on 10 targets for 81 yards through six regular-season games, but he has the opportunity Sunday to operate in an expanded role due to the absence of rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder).

items.head: Expected to play in Week 8
items.body: Ridley (hip) is in line to play in Sunday's game against the Bengals, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. After sitting out in Week 7 due to a hip injury, Ridley kicked off Week 8 prep with back-to-back limited sessions before upgrading to full Friday and entering the weekend listed as questionable. Assuming he's deemed active about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, he'll be working in a Titans receiving corps without top WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) for the first time this season.

items.head: Questionable for Week 8
items.body: Ridley (hip) is officially questionable for Sunday's matchup against Cincinnati. Ridley didn't play last week due to a hip injury, but he was able to upgrade to full practice participation this Friday. Although Tennessee hasn't cleared him to suit up against the Bengals just yet, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports that the veteran wideout is set to play. Ridley's expected return is especially timely given that No. 1 wideout Carnell Tate (shoulder) has been ruled out.

items.head: Still sidelined at practice
items.body: Montgomery (groin) remained sidelined at practice Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.

items.head: David Montgomery (Groin) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Could return to practice soon
items.body: Coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday he's hopeful that Montgomery (groin) could resume practicing this week, or next week, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports. Montgomery last saw game action in Week 5, but at this stage he appears to be inching closer to a return, with Ryans adding Monday that he's pleased with the veteran back's progress. In Montgomery's absence, Woody Marks has served as the Texans' clear-cut RB1, but once Montgomery is back, Houston's backfield time-share figures to be restored.

items.head: David Montgomery (Groin) is Out
items.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that Montgomery (groin) has made some progress but is still viewed as week-to-week and will remain out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.

items.head: Not seen at practice
items.body: Montgomery (groin) wasn't present for the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. Montgomery missed the Texans' two games before a Week 8 bye due to a groin issue, and his status remains up in the air as the team prepares for Sunday's contest at the Chargers. He hasn't practiced since sustaining the injury Oct. 11 at Tennessee, meaning he likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to suit up this weekend.

items.head: Status uncertain for Week 9
items.body: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that he has "no significant update" on the status of Montgomery (groin) heading into a Week 9 matchup with the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. Prior to the Texans' Week 8 bye, Montgomery missed two straight games due to a groin injury and wasn't able to practice in advance of either of those contests. Ryans didn't offer much of an indication that Montgomery's condition has dramatically improved following the bye, with the coach noting that the running back will be evaluated throughout the week before a decision is made on his status for Sunday's contest. If Montgomery ends up being sidelined for a third consecutive game, Woody Marks would be in store for another turn as Houston's lead back.

items.head: Expected to practice Wednesday
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) is expected to take part in Wednesday's practice, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.

items.head: Status for Week 10 remains uncertain
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) has a chance to play Sunday against San Francisco, but his practice reps will likely again be capped this week, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports. Pickens was limited in practice all of last week and ultimately didn't suit up Sunday against Indianapolis. There had been some optimism that he'd be able to participate in that contest, so there's likely a decent chance that he'll be able to return to action versus the 49ers. Nonetheless, Pickens could again be given a designation heading into this weekend if he doesn't manage at least one full practice before the Cowboys' final injury report is released Friday.

items.head: George Pickens (Hamstring) is Out
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game at Indianapolis.

items.head: Will remain limited Friday
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) "will be a little bit limited" Friday, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer is "hopeful" he will play Sunday against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Pickens was limited at practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a hamstring issue, and it appears he will find himself in a similar spot at Friday's practice. The Cowboys will provide another update on his status after the latest session comes to a close.

items.head: George Pickens (Hamstring) is Questionable
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) "will be a little bit limited" Friday, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer is "hopeful" he will play Sunday against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.head: Another limited session
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) was limited at Thursday's practice, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Pickens maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he deals with lingering shoulder and hamstring injuries. He still was able to handle a 57 percent snap share this past Sunday against the Cardinals, but he mustered only two catches (on four targets) for 48 yards. Friday's practice report will unveil whether or not Pickens heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Indianapolis.

items.head: Limited in Wednesday's practice
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports. Pickens was limited by shoulder and hamstring injuries last week, but he was able to suit up this past Sunday against the Cardinals, logging a 57 percent snap share and gathering in two of four targets for 48 yards. As Week 9 prep kicks off, he's being listed with only the hamstring issue, which continues to impact his on-field work. Pickens will have two more chances to get back to full Thursday and Friday before Dallas potentially tags him with a designation for Sunday's contest at Indianapolis.

items.head: Only two receptions in Week 8
items.body: Pickens tallied two catches (on four targets) for 48 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals. Pickens' inconsistency from week to week in 2026 continued in Week 8, as he matched his season low in receptions and ended up with his third-fewest receiving yards in a contest through the first eight games. Granted, his activity level was limited Wednesday through Friday due to shoulder and hamstring injuries, so he was operating at less than 100 percent health-wise Sunday. In any case, Pickens will strive for better results next Sunday on the road against the Colts.

items.head: Could return in 2-to-3 weeks
items.body: Jacobs will undergo surgery on his broken right ring finger later this week and could be cleared to play in as soon as 2-to-3 weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

items.head: Finger surgery on tap, IR a possibility
items.body: When asked if IR is a possibility for Jacobs (finger), coach Matt LaFleur said Monday, "I think everything is a possibility," Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, LaFleur confirmed Monday that Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured ring finger. As a result of the looming procedure, Pelissero adds that that the running back is out indefinitely, which supports the notion that an IR stint for Jacobs could be on the table.

items.head: Reportedly set for finger surgery
items.body: Jacobs is in line to undergo surgery on his injured finger this week and is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks, according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. We'll look for confirmation of this report from the Packers, but it looks like the team will be without its top back this weekend against the Vikings, at a minimum.  With MarShawn Lloyd dealing with a knee injury that sidelined him in Week 9, Kaleb Johnson profiles as Green Bay's top healthy back, with Pierre Strong also in the mix.

items.head: Josh Jacobs (Finger) is Doubtful
items.body: doubtful

items.head: Uncertain to play Week 10
items.body: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged after Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots that Jacobs' (finger) availability for the team's Week 10 matchup with the Vikings is uncertain, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports. "Hopefully we can do something to allow him to go out there," LaFleur said of Jacobs. "But he was just having a hard time gripping the ball." Jacobs was limited to just 10 snaps before leaving Sunday's game in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger while attempting to stiff-arm a defender at the end of his fourth and final carry of the day. He made two trips to the locker room with the hope of adding enough protection to his hand to enable him to return to the game, but the Packers ultimately determined that Jacobs wouldn't have been able to securely grip the football if he had checked back in. With MarShawn Lloyd (knee) inactive against the Patriots and Jacobs leaving early, Kaleb Johnson (14 carries for 68 yards) ended up finishing as the Packers' rushing leader on the day.

items.head: Packers' Josh Jacobs dealing with broken finger, status for Vikings tilt TBD
items.body: Josh Jacobs broke the ring finger on his right hand while trying to stiff-arm a defender and is unsure if he'll be able to play next week against the Vikings.

items.head: Has fractured finger
items.body: Jacobs fractured his finger during Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. Head coach Matt LaFleur revealed the nature of Jacobs' injury after the game. Jacobs exited the win with what was initially deemed a hand injury. He was unable to return against the Patriots, but the Packers are hoping Jacobs will be available for Week 10 against the Vikings. If Jacobs can't go, Pierre Strong, Kaleb Johnson and possibly MarShawn Lloyd (knee) would be Green Bay's backfield options.

items.head: Josh Jacobs (Hand) is Questionable
items.body: Jacobs (hand) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Patriots.

items.head: Browns' Monken: Watson over Sanders QB decision based on 'full body of work'
items.body: Browns coach Todd Monken said Wednesday his intention all along was to stick with Deshaun Watson as QB1 based on his "full body of work" this season.

items.head: Officially named Week 10 starter
items.body: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson (concussion) will start Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Remains in line to start Sunday
items.body: Watson (concussion) will serve as the Browns' starting quarterback in Sunday's game against the Texans, a source tells Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.

items.head: Source: Browns returning to Watson as QB1 despite Sanders' strong fill-in start
items.body: The Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 against the Texans, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.

items.head: Browns QB Deshaun Watson out of concussion protocol
items.body: Browns QB Deshaun Watson is out of the concussion protocol, but is questionable. Shedeur Sanders will get the start against the Saints.

items.head: Returns to practice field Friday
items.body: Watson (concussion) was present for practice Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network previously suggested that Watson "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, but either way, the QB's return to the field, in any capacity, is a positive step toward him advancing through the NFL's concussion protocol. Friday's final injury report will add further clarity to Watson's Week 9 status, but if he isn't cleared to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start in his place.

items.head: Not practicing Wednesday
items.body: Tate (shoulder) won't practice Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.

items.head: Carnell Tate (Shoulder) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Remains without return timeline
items.body: When asked Wednesday whether Pierce (heel) has a chance to return from IR this season, Colts head coach Shane Steichen was noncommittal, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.

items.head: No timetable for return
items.body: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports. Steichen said that Pierce, who has been on IR since Sept. 26, is currently rehabbing his injury, but the wideout's return is clearly not imminent. At 2-6, the Colts, who are already sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline, have little incentive to rush Pierce back. Meanwhile, fellow WR Josh Downs has asked to be dealt, a situation that further clouds the team's pass-catching corps ahead of Week 9.

items.head: Alec Pierce (Heel) is Injured Reserve
items.body: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.

items.head: To be limited in Wednesday's practice
items.body: Cooper (ankle) will be limited in Wednesday's practice, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.

items.head: Omar Cooper Jr. (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Eight catches in Wilson's absence
items.body: Cooper caught eight of 11 targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Cooper worked as the clear No.1 receiver for the Jets in the absence of Garrett Wilson (concussion), leading the team in targets, catches and receiving yards while Adonai Mitchell failed to catch any of his seven targets. Prior to finishing without a target in the Week 8 loss to the Raiders, Cooper delivered consecutive performances with at least 103 yards and a touchdown, so he has been effective in three of four games since returning from an IR stint due to a Week 1 ankle injury. Even if Wilson returns in Week 10, Cooper looks likely to remain involved in what could be a pass-heavy game plan against the Bills.

items.head: Primed for key role sans Wilson
items.body: Cooper and Adonai Mitchell will be the Jets' top wide receivers with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports. After back-to-back 100-yard games in his first two weeks off injured reserve, Cooper ran 26 routes last week without registering a target in the 38-33 loss to Las Vegas. Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown, also running 26 routes, and Cimini's report notes that Mitchell "will become the No. 1 receiver" in Wilson's absence. Both Mitchell and Cooper figure to get plenty of snaps and routes, but targets and production aren't as assured.

items.head: No targets in Week 8
items.body: Cooper did not garner a target during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. Cooper entered Week 8 having topped 100 receiving yards with a touchdown in back-to-back games, so Sunday's performance was especially disappointing. The rookie wideout was overshadowed by Adonai Mitchell (7-142-1) and Garrett Wilson (6-83-0) in the game, and it'll be hard to predict his workload ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup with the Chiefs.

items.head: Will help fill in for departed Allen
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen said that Dulin will be one of the Colts receivers who absorb the snaps vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports. Steichen also mentioned Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine as other candidates to fill in at the outside receiver spot opposite Laquon Treadwell, while noting that Anthony Gould will serve as the Colts' starting slot receiver after the team also traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. With Alec Pierce's (heel) return from injured reserve seemingly not imminent, Dulin could have a prime opportunity to see extended snaps over the next few weeks, provided he can hold off the likes of Burks and Westbrook-Ikhine for playing time. Dulin already made a bit of a splash in the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, connecting with Daniel Jones on a 55-yard touchdown reception while also carrying once for a three-yard gain.

items.head: Returning to limited parctice
items.body: Wilson (concussion) will be a a limited participant in Wednesday's practice,  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athleticreports. That's a step in the right direction for Wilson, who didn't practice last week before being ruled out for Week 9 action. Given that the wideout is still limited at this stage, Wilson has some hurdles to clear before he's cleared from the NFL's concussion protocol, however, if he's able return to action this weekend versus the Bills, he'll reclaim his lead role in a WR corps that was paced by Omar Cooper (ankle) and Adonai Mitchell in his absence from this past Sunday's loss to the Chiefs.

items.head: Garrett Wilson (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Garrett Wilson (Concussion) is Out
items.body: Wilson (concussion) is out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.

items.head: Not spotted at practice Thursday
items.body: Wilson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, wasn't seen at Thursday's practice, Antwan Staley of the New York Daily News reports. Wilson also logged a DNP on Wednesday, so the wideout's apparent absence from Thursday's session sets the stage for Friday's practice to loom large in terms of his availability for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. In the event that Wilson isn't cleared to play, added targets will be available for some combo of WRs Omar Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams, as well as tight ends Mason Taylor (back) and Kenyon Sadiq.

items.head: Enters concussion protocol, day-to-day
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Wilson is in the NFL's concussion protocol and is considered day-to-day,  Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports. Per Eric Allen of the Jets' official site, Wilson experienced symptoms of a concussion when he was evaluated Monday after taking a hard hit near the end of Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Jets.  As a result, Wilson won't practice Wednesday, and his status for Sunday's road game against the Chiefs will need to be tracked closely in the coming days. If Wilson ends up being sidelined this weekend, added targets could be available for wideouts Omar Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams and tight ends Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq.

items.head: Targeted 12 times in Week 8 loss
items.body: Wilson caught six of 12 targets for 83 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders. Wilson saw his second-highest target total of the season Sunday after being targeted a season-low three times in the Week 7 loss to Miami. After being outplayed by Omar Cooper in each of the previous two games, Wilson took a back seat to Adonai Mitchell in this one, as Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown while Cooper went without a target. The Jets have three capable wide receivers for the first time in a while, but Wilson easily leads the team with 527 receiving yards heading into a Week 9 road game against the Chiefs, while Mitchell's a distant second with 265 receiving yards.

items.head: Gets QB upgrade at deadline
items.body: Jefferson stands to benefit from Tuesday's acquisition of Kirk Cousins, who is expected to take over as the Vikings' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game against the Packers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports. Jefferson had averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 and 8.5 touchdowns per season. Though Cousins is three years older from when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and underwhelming receiver group.

items.head: Highly inefficient sans Murray
items.body: Jefferson brought in three of 11 targets for 58 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.

items.head: Inside Justin Jefferson's miraculous catch for Vikings versus Bills in 2022
items.body: In 2022 against the Bills, Jefferson leaped up and came down with one of "the greatest catches of all time."

items.head: Justin Jefferson (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Picturesque TD catch in loss
items.body: Jefferson brought in five of nine targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Jefferson led the Vikings in receptions with the aid of a team-high target total, and the highlight of the perennial Pro Bowler's afternoon was his touchdown grab. Jefferson stuck his hand up and tapped Kyler Murray's (hamstring) pass to himself while in tight coverage in the left corner of the end zone early in the second quarter, ultimately securing a memorable one-yard score. Jefferson has topped 50 receiving yards just three times and is still in search of his first 100-yard game of the season, but he's found the end zone in two of the last three games heading into a Week 9 home showdown against the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9.

items.head: Denzel Boston (Toe) is Questionable
items.body: Boston isn't expected to practice Wednesday due to a toe injury, Daniel Oyefusi reports.

items.head: Just misses century mark in New Orleans
items.body: Boston caught six of seven targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. The 98 yards led the Browns on the afternoon, and Boston showed some immediate chemistry with Shedeur Sanders, connecting with the QB on a 60-yard strike in the third quarter that nearly resulted in a touchdown. The rookie receiver was also the target on a two-point conversion attempt that would have won the game in OT, but the pass got broken up. Boston also set a new career high in receiving yards with the performance, and if Sanders takes over for Deshaun Watson (concussion) under center on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays. Through his first nine NFL games. Boston's delivered a 32-507-3 line on 61 targets.

items.head: Cleared for Sunday
items.body: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports. With Boston upgrading from limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday to full participation Friday, he should be fine for his usual role as a near-every-down player in a young Cleveland offense. It'll be his first chance to work with Shedeur Sanders extensively outside of a practice environment, as the Browns reportedly won't start Deshaun Watson (head) even if he clears concussion protocol before the game.

items.head: Denzel Boston (injury) is Active
items.body: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Boston (calf) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. Boston dealt with a foot issue a couple weeks ago, but the calf injury is new this week. The rookie wideout has been scuffling after a hot start to the season. Perhaps the likely insertion of Shedeur Sanders this Sunday against the Saints can help Boston regain his big-play ability. Boston is a low-floor, upside WR4 for fantasy.

items.head: Denzel Boston (Calf) is Questionable
items.body: Boston (calf) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.

items.head: Limited by calf injury Wednesday
items.body: Boston was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports. Boston made appearances on the injury report in Weeks 6 and 7 due to a foot issue, but he's tending to a new health concern coming out of this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. The rookie wideout will have two more chances this week to upgrade to full practice, and if he does, he should head into Sunday's game in New Orleans without an injury designation.

items.head: Six snags in loss
items.body: Boston caught six of 11 targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. Boston entered Week 8 having caught just four of 13 targets for 42 yards over the previous two games, so Sunday's output was a step in the right direction. The wide receiver's 11 targets were a new career high, and he ranked second behind tight end Harold Fannin (12) in the category versus Pittsburgh. Boston has now reeled in 26 of 53 targets for 409 yards and three touchdowns over the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

items.head: Stepping into slot role
items.body: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Gould is in line to step into the slot role previously held by Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. With both Downs and Keenan Allen having been dealt by the Colts on Tuesday, the team will be operating with a re-shaped WR corps going forward. According to the Colts' latest unofficial depth chart, Gould is indeed listed a first-teamer along with Ashton Dulin and Laquon Treadwell. Also expected to have additional opportunities in the coming weeks will be 2026 seventh-rounder Deion Burks, with veteran pass-catcher Nick Westbrook-Ikhine in the mix as well after being signed off the practice squad. Though a wait-and-see approach is in order in term's of Gould's fantasy lineup viability, his production beginning this weekend versus Miami is worth tracking by those in deeper PPR formats.

items.head: Anthony Gould (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Sources: Giants called Falcons to ask about Bijan Robinson before trade deadline
items.body: The Giants made a call to the Falcons before the NFL trade deadline inquiring about star running back Bijan Robinson, multiple sources told ESPN.

items.head: Big workload in loss to Cincy
items.body: Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he's gotten into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.

items.head: Manages solid rushing total in shutout
items.body: Robinson rushed 19 times for 76 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Falcons' 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday. It was a bizarre afternoon overall in very rainy conditions in Tampa Bay, and Robinson managed to salvage his day with a solid rushing yardage total. Robinson's tally on the ground was actually his best since Week 5, although his streak of games without a rushing touchdown extended to four. Robinson is still averaging 5.2 yards per carry on the season and now is up to 983 yards from scrimmage and five total touchdowns heading into next Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Bengals in Madrid.

items.head: Back to No. 2 role in Week 10
items.body: Sanders will return to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Texans after the Browns announced Wednesday that Deshaun Watson (concussion) will draw the Week 10 start, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports. Watson led the Browns to a 5-3 record over their first eight games before developing concussion symptoms and being placed in the NFL's five-step protocol last week. Though Watson cleared protocol last Saturday, his lack of on-field reps during the week prompted the Browns to keep him inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Saints. Sanders stepped in under center and overcame a slow start to finish with 297 passing yards, 28 rushing yards, two passing touchdowns and no turnovers in a 23-22 overtime loss, with his performance drawing praise from head coach Todd Monken. Though the Browns will go back to a healthy Watson for Week 10, Sanders' strong outing in New Orleans could put Watson on shakier ground atop the depth chart.

items.head: Nearly leads Browns to OT win
items.body: Sanders completed 19 of 31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added 28 yards on 10 carries. Making his first start of the season in place of Deshaun Watson (concussion), Sanders put together an impressive performance, hitting KC Concepcion for a 64-yard TD late in the fourth quarter and then connecting with Harold Fannin for a 39-yard score in OT. Todd Monken elected to go for the win with a two-point conversion rather than giving the ball back to New Orleans, but Sanders' attempt to hit Denzel Boston in the corner of the end zone failed, although the play would have been wiped out by a holding call anyway. Even if Watson is deemed ready to go ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Texans, Sanders' strong showing may have given his coach something to think about.

items.head: Browns coach 'proud' of Shedeur Sanders but sidesteps questions on QB position
items.body: Browns coach Todd Monken said he was "proud" of Shedeur Sanders' performance in Cleveland's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints but refused to answer whether Sanders made a case to start going forward.

items.head: 3 ways Browns QB Shedeur Sanders can show growth vs. Saints
items.body: The opportunity is a big one as the second-year quarterback's first start of the season comes at a critical time.

items.head: Will start Sunday
items.body: Sanders will start at quarterback Sunday against the Saints, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports. Coach Todd Monken said the move is because Deshaun Watson (concussion) missed so much practice time this week. Watson has been one of the worst statistical quarterbacks in the league over the last month, so Sanders could potentially keep the job if he has a good game against the Saints. His insertion under center doesn't change the outlook of the offense, as both Watson and Sanders are game-manager types.

items.head: Browns to start Sanders at QB vs. Saints with Watson in protocol
items.body: The Browns will start Shedeur Sanders at quarterback against the Saints as Deshaun Watson remains in the concussion protocol.

items.head: Could start Week 9 with Watson in protocol
items.body: Sanders could be needed to start Sunday's game at New Orleans after Deshaun Watson was placed in concussion protocol when he experienced symptoms Monday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. During this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson briefly departed the game in the first quarter after a helmet-to-helmet hit from safety Jaquan Brisker. Sanders checked in and completed both of his pass attempts for two yards across four total plays before Watson was cleared to return for the Browns' next possession. However, with the concussion symptoms surfacing a day later, Watson's availability for Week 9 is now in jeopardy. Watson will still have time to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Sunday, but expect Sanders to at least get some reps in with the first-team offense Wednesday during the team's first practice of the week.

items.head: May be tracking for Week 14 or 15 return
items.body: The Rams remain optimistic that Nacua (knee/toe) will be able to return to action Week 14 versus the 49ers or Week 15 versus the Cowboys, Dan Graziano of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Puka Nacua (Knee - MCL) is Doubtful
items.body: doubtful

items.head: Rams WR Puka Nacua likely to hit IR with MCL/PCL sprain, turf toe
items.body: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua is likely going on injured reserve due to an MCL/PCL sprain as well as turf toe, according to head coach Sean McVay.

items.head: Sources: Puka Nacua set for tests on late-game knee injury; Rams believe ACL OK
items.body: The Rams do not believe Puka Nacua suffered a torn ACL, but the imaging Monday will tell more, sources said.

items.head: Will have MRI on knee Monday
items.body: Nacua suffered a knee injury during Sunday's 20-13 win at Washington and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine its extent, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. The Rams already are without WR Davante Adams for a few more weeks after he underwent surgery on his left hamstring, and the team now may be sans Nacua if the results of Monday's testing go a certain way. L.A. doesn't believe that Nacua sustained a torn ACL, but the MRI will reveal what type of damage he incurred. Before picking up the injury on the Rams' final offensive snap, Nacua gathered in 14 of 19 targets for 150 yards and one touchdown and took two carries for 20 yards.

items.head: Puka Nacua (Knee) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Returns after brief exit
items.body: Nacua returned to Sunday's game against the Commanders after visiting the medical tent, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports. Nacua was evaluated after sustaining an unspecified injury, but his absence wound up being brief. Barring another issue, he appears to be good to go for the remainder of Sunday's contest.

items.head: Busy day in Week 8 win
items.body: Nacua secured 11 of 12 targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday. Nacua unsurprisingly led the Rams across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets and did so by a wide margin. With Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) unavailable for the last two games, Nacua has drawn 22 total targets and scored twice, with Sunday's touchdown coming on an 18-yard catch-and-run in the latter portion of the third quarter. Nacua is being used in a shorter-area role than past seasons -- he's averaging a career-low 10.1 yards per catch -- but he'll remain an elite fantasy option in a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

items.head: NFL Week 10 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips, post-trade deadline news
items.body: No deals for Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones or Brian Thomas Jr.? Vikings seeking QB answers with their Kirk Cousins trade? Here's the latest intel.

items.head: Sticking around in Indy
items.body: The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

items.head: Set to play Sunday amid trade rumors
items.body: Taylor was a full participant at Thursday's practice, and Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports that both Taylor and head coach Shane Steichen have maintained that Taylor will play Sunday against the Cowboys despite ongoing trade rumors surrounding the star running back. "You can't avoid it," Taylor said of the trade rumors. "But it's more about trying to block that out." Taylor's preparing for what could well be his last game as a member of the Colts. Per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, the 2-6 Colts have received trade calls on numerous players including Taylor, but Indianapolis doesn't intend to complete any additional trades prior to the conclusion of Sunday's game.

items.head: Logs 12 touches in potential swan song
items.body: Taylor rushed eight times for 23 yards and brought in four of five targets for 24 yards in the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Taylor opened the game in his usual starting role with trade rumors swirling around him, and the star running back finished with a wholly unremarkable performance. Taylor ultimately ceded plenty of snaps to backfield mates Seth McGowan and DJ Giddens, the likeliest heir-apparent candidates if Taylor is indeed moved to another team in the coming days. Taylor had exceeded 90 rushing yards in back-to-back games and on five occasions overall heading into Week 8, so even if his Colts tenure finishes with Sunday's whimper, he'll have plenty to offer in a new destination.

items.head: Trade talks heating up
items.body: Taylor is being made available via trade by the Colts, Adam Schefter of ESPN  reports. Taylor himself was not requesting a trade earlier in the week, but Indianapolis' recent flurry of moves opened the possibility that the star running back would also be moved in the team's teardown before a rebuild. The Colts moved on from Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and got significant draft capital from the Seahawks and 49ers in return. Now a market is forming for Taylor, 27, who could help put a contender over the top. Per Schefter, the Colts are seeking a deal similar to what the Panthers got in 2022 when they traded Christian McCaffrey.

items.head: NFL Week 10 latest intel, buzz questions, fantasy tips, post-trade deadline news
items.body: No deals for Jonathan Taylor, Daniel Jones or Brian Thomas Jr.? Vikings seeking QB answers with their Kirk Cousins trade? Here's the latest intel.

items.head: RB Jonathan Taylor, QB Daniel Jones remain with Colts as trade deadline passes
items.body: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor and QB Daniel Jones were the subject of trade overtures in recent days and weeks but were not traded before Tuesday's trade deadline.

items.head: Pedestrian numbers in loss
items.body: Jones completed 20 of 34 passes for 180 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding three rushes for 11 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. Jones took a pair of sacks and averaged a modest 5.3 yards per attempt in what would have to be termed a disappointing performance overall considering the struggles the Cowboys defense had endured. Jones' one touchdown pass came on a 55-yard catch-and-run off a wide receiver screen by Ashton Dulin late in the third quarter. Jones has now failed to eclipse 180 passing yards in three straight games while also tossing six interceptions over his last four contests, and reports emerged late in the week that the Colts were fielding calls from multiple teams about a potential trade for the veteran signal-caller before Tuesday's deadline.

items.head: Colts in Daniel Jones trade talks as multiple teams call about QB, sources say
items.body: The Colts have engaged in trade discussions with multiple teams involving QB Daniel Jones, sources told NFL Network and ESPN.

items.head: Sticking as starting quarterback
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen said that Jones will remain the Colts' starting quarterback heading into Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports. After a 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday during which Jones was benched in favor of Anthony Richardson in the fourth quarter, Steichen suggested that he would evaluate every position, including quarterback. While some changes could still be afoot for the 2-6 Colts, Steichen will apparently stand pat at center with Jones, at least for one more week. After a promising first season in Indianapolis was cut short by a torn Achilles, Jones has been a major disappointment since reaching a two-year, $88 million extension with the Colts in March. Through eight games, Jones ranks 29th among 30 qualified quarterbacks in QBR (39.6) and is tied with the Chargers' Justin Herbert for the NFL lead with 12 turnovers (nine interceptions, three lost fumbles).

items.head: May lose starting job
items.body: Head coach Shane Steichen said after Sunday's 42-7 loss at Jacksonville that he'll evaluate "everything, including whether" Jones remains the Colts' starting quarterback, James Boyd of The Athletic reports. Jones completed 19 of 28 passes for 144 yards, one touchdown (to WR Josh Downs) and two interceptions while rushing four times for seven yards in Week 8. He also yielded the Colts' final three drives to backup QB Anthony Richardson, who didn't fare much better (2-for-2 passing for eight yards, two rushes for four yards). Sunday's performance marked Jones' fourth (in eight appearances) in which he didn't reach 200 yards passing, and overall he's sitting on a 5:9 TD:INT on the campaign. Indianapolis is in the midst of a fire sale of its active roster, and handing the keys to the offense to Richardson to see how he looks in the second half may be in the cards.

items.head: Where does Cam Ward stand coming out of the bye?
items.body: Ward has nine games left to convince the Titans he should be their QB when they open the new stadium in 2027.

items.head: First 300-yard passing game in OT loss
items.body: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He added seven rushing attempts for 41 yards, lost a fumble, ran in a two-point conversion and threw a successful two-point conversion. Ward threw two go-ahead touchdown passes in the fourth quarter, connecting with Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score before finding Wan'Dale Robinson for a 15-yard TD. Those two touchdown passes came after a streak of five Tony Pollard rushing touchdowns without a Ward passing TD over the previous seven quarters. Pollard's second rushing touchdown Sunday was followed up by a two-point conversion from Ward on the ground, and Ward threw a two-point conversion to Gunnar Helm after the touchdown pass to Robinson to take a 36-29 lead. The Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown, and Cincinnati scored to begin overtime. Tennessee's ensuing drive in OT resulted in a turnover on downs, but the bonus possession helped Ward reach 300 passing yards in a game for the first time in his career. Ward's first multi-touchdown passing performance of the season improves his TD:INT to 6:5 heading into a Week 10 home game against the Jaguars following Tennessee's Week 9 bye.

items.head: Doesn't get into Week 9 win
items.body: Wilson didn't log any snaps during Sunday's win over the Cardinals. Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.

items.head: Relegated to special teams Monday
items.body: Wilson played just seven snaps -- all on special teams -- in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears. After logging double-digit carries in six of the Seahawks' previous seven games while scoring four touchdowns and averaging 66.4 scrimmage yards during that span, Wilson fell out of the game plan entirely in Week 8. With Zach Charbonnet (knee) getting cleared to make his 2026 debut, Jadarian Price (chest) returning from injured reserve and George Holani still on hand as an option on passing downs, the Seahawks had no reps available out of the backfield for Wilson. Unless Charbonnet or Price succumbs to another injury, Wilson's playing time on offense will likely remain scarce moving forward.

items.head: More competition for work
items.body: Wilson is welcoming back Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) to the Seahawks backfield for Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Seattle cleared Charbonnet to make his season debut on its final Week 8 injury report before the team activated Price from injured reserve Monday, which means the latter is available for his first game action since Week 3. Wilson operated as the Seahawks' lead runner the last four contests, racking up 85 touches for 359 yards from scrimmage and four total TDs. He'll certainly cede some of those reps to the combination of Charbonnet and Price, but the possibility exists that he ends up taking on the most work among the trio if the team eases one or both back in.

items.head: Three grabs vs. Arizona
items.body: Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday. All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (oblique), but the former is dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. If that were the case, then Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the production floors of Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.

items.head: Scores TD on only Week 8 reception
items.body: Kupp caught one of three targets for a seven-yard touchdown Monday in a loss to the Bears. Kupp had another low target share, but he at least made the most of his only catch by hauling in a seven-yard TD early in the fourth quarter. That score probably isn't going to be enough to inspire confidence in him in fantasy, though, given that the veteran wideout has drawn three or fewer targets in six of his eight games this season. Kupp's seven receiving yards Monday also were a season-low mark, and there simply doesn't seem to be much room for any wideout aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba to regularly find success in Seattle's offense given Smith-Njigba's massive target share. With that said, Kupp at least will have a favorable matchup in Week 9, as he'll face an Arizona defense that has surrendered 11 receiving TDs to wideouts this season, tied for the most in the NFL.

items.head: Limited to special teams vs. Tampa Bay
items.body: Johnson recorded two tackles on special teams during the Bears' 27-24 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) was inactive for a fifth consecutive game, with Johnson operating as the Bears' RB2 behind D'Andre Swift in the Bears' four contests prior to Sunday against the Bucs. However, Johnson didn't play a single offensive snap against Tampa Bay; instead, it was Salvon Ahmed (five carries for 25 yards) who mixed into the backfield as Chicago's complementary piece to Swift. The Bears are on a bye for Week 10, with their next game taking place in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22. Johnson would have a narrow path to offensive relevancy if Monangai is cleared to return for that contest.

items.head: Four catches in SNF win
items.body: Raymond caught four passes for 32 yards on seven targets in Sunday night's 27-24 win over the Bucs. Raymond tied Rome Odunze for second on the team in targets behind Luther Burden (nine), but Burden was injured late in the fourth quarter. If he needs to miss any time, Raymond projects to see elevated snaps alongside Odunze and Colston Loveland. The good news for Burden is he'll have two weeks to heal up with the Bears headed into their bye.

items.head: Racks up 53 total yards on MNF
items.body: Raymond finished Monday's 34-17 win against Seattle with two catches for 14 yards on three targets along with one rush for 39 yards. Raymond's most memorable contribution was a 39-yard dash on a third-down play early in the fourth quarter to take the ball down to Seattle's five-yard line and set up a D'Andre Swift touchdown. Though he didn't put up massive numbers, Raymond's 53 total yards were his most since Week 3 and represented more yardage than he had recorded over his previous four games combined. Raymond remains a shaky fantasy play given his recent numbers, and a Week 9 matchup against a Tampa Bay defense that has been pretty stingy on wideouts doesn't improve his outlook.

items.head: One catch against Seattle
items.body: Virgil caught one of four targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday. Gardner Minshew found Virgil for a 25-yard pass early in the first quarter, but the duo failed to connect with each other for the rest of Sunday's contest. The Cardinals' offense took quite a hit in Week 9, with Minshew sustaining a torn UCL and wide receiver Michael Wilson suffering a fracture in his neck, and those injuries will keep both players on the shelf for the rest of the 2026 season. Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are both also on season-ending IR, which leaves Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay and superstar tight end Trey McBride as the top targets for rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck heading into Week 10 against the Rams.

items.head: Two catches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Dotson caught two passes for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Despite playing 84 percent of the offensive snaps, Dotson's two targets were a distant sixth on the team against Cincinnati. He has 16 catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets through nine games this season and isn't a particularly exciting fantasy option fighting for scraps behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta.

items.head: Secures two catches in loss
items.body: Dotson caught two of five targets for 95 yards during Sunday's 16-0 loss to Tampa Bay. Dotson and the rest of the Falcons offense were held in check for the majority of Sunday's loss. The wide receiver did provide Atlanta's biggest highlight play of the day, connecting with quarterback Michael Penix for a 76-yard gain on the team's final possession of the day in the fourth quarter. Dotson's 95 yards were a season high, and he has now reeled in 14 of 31 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

items.head: Two grabs versus Seattle
items.body: Higgins caught both of his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. With all of the injuries at wide receiver for Arizona, Higgins played a season-high 66 percent of the offensive snaps in Seattle. It still didn't translate to an elevated role in the pass game. Higgins has 18 grabs for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets across nine games this season.

items.head: Logs one carry against Green Bay
items.body: Larison recorded a four-yard rush and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles (one solo) on special teams. Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. It was Larison has seen little activity in the Patriots' offense over the team's last two games, but that could change given that Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to be out for "the next few weeks" due to a knee injury he sustained Sudnay, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

items.head: Just one catch in Week 9 victory
items.body: Higbee caught one of five targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. Higbee was held to just one catch for a second consecutive game, although his 13-yard grab set the Rams up on the Commanders' one yard line and led to a rushing touchdown by Blake Corum on the next play. Higbee has only four catches over his last three games, but he figures to play a larger role in the passing game for at least the next month while Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is on injured reserve. The Rams will hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up six touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL.

items.head: Another quiet performance Week 8
items.body: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory. Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).

items.head: Produces 52 yards in Week 9 loss
items.body: Raridon caught three passes for 52 yards on six targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers. Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.

items.head: Quiet Sunday despite extended opportunity
items.body: Raridon had one reception for five yards on four targets in New England's 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Raridon's lone reception went for five yards early in the first quarter. He didn't record another catch for the remainder of the contest despite logging a hefty 93 percent offensive snap share, largely due to No .1 tight end Hunter Henry departing in the first half due to a foot injury. Should Henry remain sidelined in Week 9, Raridon will have another big opportunity to produce in a home tilt against Green Bay.

items.head: Draws five targets in Week 9 win
items.body: Atwell recorded two catches on five targets for 16 yards during the Rams' 20-13 win over the Commanders on Sunday. Atwell ended up finishing second among Rams wide receivers in both targets and offensive snaps behind Puka Nacua. However, the Rams' offense will have to undergo a sizable overhaul in the absence of Nacua, who suffered a sprained PCL/MCL in his knee as well as turf toe during Sunday's win, with the superstar wide receiver expected to be sidelined for at least a month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. Davante Adams (hamstring) is also on injured reserve, so that leaves Atwell and Konata Mumpfield as the top healthy wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster, and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels is also in position for a larger role on offense. The Rams will face the Cardinals in Week 10, and Arizona's defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns on the year, which is second-most in the league behind Las Vegas' 20.

items.head: Brings in two passes vs. Washington
items.body: Mumpfield caught both of his targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. Despite the lack of production, Mumpfield's 20 receiving yards ended up being second-most on the Rams behind Puka Nacua (150). The bigger news from Sunday's game was Nacua sustaining a PCL/MCL sprain in his knee and turf toe, and the superstar wide receiver is expected to miss at least one month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. With Davante Adams (hamstring) also on IR until at least Week 11, that leaves the Rams with Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels as the top wide receivers for Matthew Stafford. The Rams hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns, which is second-most in the NFL behind the Raiders (20).

items.head: Tallies two catches against Las Vegas
items.body: Cooks brought in both of his targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. Cooks and other 49ers wide receivers operated in elevated roles Sunday due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 25 receiving yards ended up being third-most on the Niners behind Jordan Watkins (86) and tight end George Kittle (58), and Cooks' 32 offensive snaps were also third-most among San Francisco wide receivers. The 49ers hit the road for Week 10 against the Cowboys, and Cooks' workload on offense would decrease if one or both of Evans or Samuel was cleared to return.

items.head: Totals 36 yards against Houston
items.body: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets. The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

items.head: Leads team in rushing in loss
items.body: Vidal rushed eight times for 23 yards and caught both of his targets for seven yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. The Chargers continue to use a fantasy-unfriendly three-man backfield, giving all three of Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell meaningful touches and snaps. In a broken Los Angeles offense and crowded group of RBs, Vidal has minimal fantasy appeal outside of deeper formats.

items.head: Blanked in Week 9
items.body: Treadwell logged 52 of the Colts' 64 snaps and was held without a reception on one target in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Since drawing a season-high eight targets in a Week 5 loss to the Steelers, Treadwell has barely surpassed that total over the past four games combined. Despite handling snap shares north of 70 percent in each of those contests, Treadwell has mustered a 5-58-0 receiving line on 10 targets during that stretch. The Colts will have more target volume up for grabs after trading Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday, and though Treadwell could be one of the beneficiaries, he still looks to be a low-upside fantasy option.

items.head: Only two catches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

items.head: Five snags in defeat
items.body: Gadsden caught all five of his targets for 52 yards during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. Gadsden was able to lead the team in catches while he finished with one fewer target than team leader Ladd McConkey. The tight end has now reeled in at least three passes for the second straight game and third time over the last four contests after having failed to do so in any of the team's first three regular-season games. Gadsden and the rest of the Chargers will face a tough test in Week 9 against the Texans.

items.head: Active in Week 8
items.body: Gadsden is active for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Rams. The second-year tight end has had a relatively quiet first season to date in coordinator Mike McDaniel's offense, posting a 12-103-1 line on 21 targets through six games. Gadsden did get back on the Chargers' offense's radar before the Week 7 bye, recording three receptions for 17 yards on five targets over 33 snaps in Week 6 against the Chiefs after being blanked over 39 plays in Week 5 against the Broncos. It remains to be seen if Los Angeles, which declined to make a change at playcaller during the bye, cooked up some improvements during the idle week, and if Gadsden will be more involved moving forward after flashing plenty of upside as a rookie in 2025 with a 49-664-3 line across 15 regular-season contests.

items.head: Tallies three catches against Houston
items.body: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

items.head: One catch against Rams
items.body: Kolar caught one of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams. The tight end's four targets tied for third on the team, as he ran 17 routes on Justin Herbert's 37 dropbacks against Los Angeles. More of a blocker than receiver, Kolar has been forced to catch more passes out of necessity at times this season. He has 10 grabs for 98 yards on 17 targets. The catches and targets are both career highs in his fifth season.

items.head: Coach non-committal on Week 10 return
items.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that the Saints haven't yet determined whether Etienne (hamstring) will return from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports. "We'll see," Moore said. "He's progressing well. We'll gather some more information and make a decision."

items.head: Not practicing yet
items.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints haven't opened Etienne's (hamstring) practice window just yet, Jeff Nowak of WWL Louisiana reports. Etienne has missed the required four games on IR due to a strained left hamstring, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he hasn't gained clearance to mix into drills. Moore told Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana on Monday that Etienne has a chance to return to practice this week, but with no on-field work to begin Week 9 prep, he seems to be on the outside looking in to have enough time to be activated for Sunday's contest against the Browns.

items.head: Travis Etienne Jr. (Hamstring) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints haven't opened Etienne's (hamstring) practice window just yet, Jeff Nowak of WWL Louisiana reports.

items.head: Chance to practice in Week 9
items.body: Head coach Kellen Moore said that Etienne (hamstring) will be evaluated Monday before the Saints make a determination whether he practices this week, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports. Sidelined since he sustained a left hamstring strain in a Sept. 27 loss to the Raiders, Etienne will be eligible to play coming out of the Saints' Week 8 bye now that he's missed the required four games while on injured reserve. If Etienne looks good during his upcoming evaluation, he could have his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, when the Saints will begin prepping for Sunday's game against the Browns. Given the time that he's missed, Etienne might need to practice fully at some point this week for the Saints to feel comfortable activating him after a minimum-length stint on IR.

items.head: Turns in full practice
items.body: Okonkwo (hip) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice. Now that he's gotten a full practice under his belt this week, Okonkwo should be in the clear for Thursday's game against the Giants. The veteran tight end has emerged a more integral part of the Washington passing game over the last four games, having cleared 70 percent snap shares in each of those contests while putting together a 19-218-0 receiving line on 24 targets.

items.head: Dealing with hip issue
items.body: Okonkwo was deemed a limited participant on Washington's estimated practice report Monday due to a hip injury, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Okonkwo appears to have gotten hurt in Sunday's loss to the Rams, though he logged his usual offensive snap share (74 percent) and finished with s solid 6-57-0 receiving line on seven targets. The Commanders didn't actually practice Monday, so the tight end's level of activity -- if any -- Tuesday should provide more clarity about whether he's at risk of missing Thursday's clash against the Giants. Washington has been hurt by injuries to its wideout corps, and Okonkwo has stepped up with 57 or more receiving yards in three of the team's past four games.

items.head: Chig Okonkwo (Hip) is Questionable
items.body: Okonkwo caught six of seven targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams.

items.head: Six snags in loss
items.body: Okonkwo caught six of seven targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. Okonkwo finished tied for the team lead in targets with wide receiver Van Jefferson, reeling in at least five passes for the second time in three games. The tight end's seven targets matched a season high, and he is still searching for his first touchdown as a member of the Commanders after joining the team in the offseason.

items.head: Musters two catches in Week 8
items.body: Okonkwo tallied two catches (on four targets) for 32 yards during Sunday's 27-10 win versus the Eagles. Okonkwo logged a typical 77 percent snap share in Week 8, but aside from a stellar 21-yard catch in the fourth quarter, he didn't contribute much to the Commanders offense. Overall, he's mustered just a 17-182-0 line on 24 targets in his five appearances this season, but 15 of his catches have occurred in the four full contests for Jayden Daniels in 2026, so the tight end has exhibited a rapport with the team's primary signal-caller. Okonkwo will aim for a bounceback this coming Sunday against the Rams.

items.head: Upgrades to full practice
items.body: Mooney (chest) was a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice, Mooney took every rep a day later to erase any concern about his status heading into Thursday's game against the Commanders. The veteran wideout has played more than 50 percent of the offensive snaps in all but one of the Giants' eight games to date, but he exceeded two receptions and 50 receiving yards for the first time all season in this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. He remains a relatively unappealing fantasy option while receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely are locked in as the Giants' clear top two pass catchers.

items.head: Considered limited Monday
items.body: Mooney (chest) was estimated to be a limited participant at the Giants' walkthrough practice Monday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports. Mooney reeled in a season-high three passes for 54 yards and also had a rush for minus-4 yards during Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. The wide receiver may have picked up a chest injury during the victory, and as a result, he was considered to be less than 100 percent Monday. Mooney will have two more chances to be upgraded to a full participant prior to Thursday night's matchup with the Commanders.

items.head: Darnell Mooney (Chest) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.body: The Chiefs have acquired needed help at wide receiver, acquiring Josh Downs in a trade with the Colts, sources told ESPN and NFL Network.

items.head: On move to Kansas City
items.body: The Chiefs acquired Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Colts on Tuesday in exchange for 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

items.head: 2026 NFL trade deadline updates: Josh Downs, Kirk Cousins on the move
items.body: The NFL trade deadline is at 4 p.m. ET. We're following all the action, including the Chiefs trading for Josh Downs.

items.head: Another forgettable Week 9 line
items.body: Downs caught three of six targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Downs has now failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of his last six games, as he's settled in as a pedestrian slot receiver in an Indianapolis offense that makes very few plays in the passing game. The 25-year-old has requested a trade ahead of Tuesday's deadline, but the Colts haven't received much interest by most accounts. Downs' rest-of-season fate will be clearer after the trade deadline.

items.head: Multi-drop game in Colts' loss irks WR Josh Downs as trade deadline looms
Reaches paydirt in Week 8
items.body: Downs caught four of five targets for 23 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars. Downs was able to reel in four or more passes for the fourth time this season and second time in the last three weeks. Downs was on the receiving end of the team's only score on the day, grabbing a six-yard touchdown pass from Daniel Jones in the third quarter for the wideout's first score of the year. Downs has now caught 30 of 51 targets for 330 yards and a touchdown over eight contests to open the 2026 campaign, and after he requested a trade this week, he may be wearing a new uniform the next time he appears in a game.

items.head: Stone Smartt (Undisclosed) is Questionable

items.head: Cut loose by Philly
items.body: The Eagles waived Blue on Tuesday. Philadelphia is now left with Saquon Barkley as the lone running back on its 53-man roster, but Elijah Mitchell will most likely be signed off the practice squad to replace Blue. After being signed off the practice squad himself in late October, Blue suited up in the Eagles' last two games but played just eight total snaps on offense while recording no rushing attempts and a nine-yard reception. His main contributions came on special teams, where he served as the Eagles' primary kickoff returner and gained 268 yards on 12 runbacks (22.3 average).

items.head: Michael Wilson (Neck) is Injured Reserve

items.head: Cardinals WR Michael Wilson (neck) to miss rest of season
items.body: Cardinals wide receiver Michael Wilson will miss the rest of the season after suffering a neck fracture on the fourth play of Sunday's game that he played through.

items.head: Michael Wilson (Neck) is Out
items.body: Wilson notched six catches (on seven targets) for 60 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss in Seattle.

items.head: Paces Cardinals in receiving
items.body: Wilson notched six catches (on seven targets) for 60 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss in Seattle. Wilson has been tending to two broken ribs the last two games, and he also was working with new starting QB Gardner Minshew after the Cardinals dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens this past week. Nonetheless, Wilson led Arizona in receiving yards, marking the fourth time he's reached 60 such yards in the last seven contests en route to a 38-412-2 line on 67 targets during that stretch. Wilson will look to improve his rapport with Minshew -- and also get healthier -- next Sunday versus the Rams.

items.head: No designation for Week 9
items.body: Wilson (rest/ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest in Seattle, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Wilson has worn a yellow non-contact jersey in practice the last two weeks due to two broken ribs that has contained him to limited sessions. Having said that, he'll continue to play through the concern as he did this past Sunday in Dallas, when he hauled in eight of 15 targets for 111 yards and one touchdown and took one carry for 17 yards on a 79 percent snap share.

items.head: Stays limited in practice
items.body: Wilson (rest/ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports. Wilson continues to don a yellow non-contact jersey on the practice field as he deals with two broken ribs, so his activity level comes as no surprise. Friday's injury report will determine if Wilson enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Seattle, but he's already demonstrated an ability to play through the issue, notching a 79 percent snap share, reeling in eight of 15 targets for 111 yards and one touchdown and recording a 17-yard carry in this past Sunday's win in Dallas.

items.head: Michael Wilson (Ribs) is Questionable
items.body: Wilson (rest/ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

items.head: Still in non-contact jersey
items.body: Wilson (ribs) remained in a yellow non-contact jersey at Thursday's practice, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports. Wilson has been wearing said jersey the past two weeks due to what he noted are two broken ribs. He still played through the pain this past Sunday in Dallas, despite exiting for a spell in the middle of the contest, ending Week 8 with eight catches (on 15 targets) for 111 yards and one touchdown and one carry for 17 yards. Thursday's injury report will unveil Wilson's activity level.

items.head: Giants' Nabers calls Fox analyst Olsen's body language critique a 'lie'
items.body: Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers said Tuesday he posted on social media after the game because he thought the critique from Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen about his body language and being a bad teammate was a "lie."

items.head: Giants' Malik Nabers takes issue with Greg Olsen, Fox for comments during game
items.body: Malik Nabers took the issue with Fox play-by-play man Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen for criticizing his body language during the Giants' win Sunday.

items.head: Quiet in Week 9 win
items.body: Nabers caught five of eight targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Nabers recorded at least 111 receiving yards in four consecutive games prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye but failed to extend that streak in Sunday's low-scoring win, during which J.J. McCarthy (hip) and Jameis Winston combined to throw for just 198 yards. The star wide receiver led the team with eight targets but finished third in receiving yards behind Darnell Mooney (54) and Isaiah Likely (53). Nabers had his hands on what would have been a 20-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter but failed to secure a diving catch attempt. McCarthy left in the third quarter but managed to return later in the second half, and he can be tentatively penciled in as the starting QB for Thursday's home game against the leaky Commanders pass defense.

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia. Nabers was held out of drills Thursday due to a knee injury, but his return to all activity one day later lines up with head coach John Harbaugh's assessment of the situation Friday, when he told Matt Citak of the Giants' official site that the wide receiver "practiced fully" and is "full go" for Week 9. As a result, Nabers will look to build upon the massive 36-509-2 line on 51 targets that he's accrued over the last four contests.

items.head: Malik Nabers (injury) is Active
items.body: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

items.head: 'Full go' for Week 9
items.body: Head coach John Harbaugh said Nabers (knee) "practiced fully" Friday and will be "full go" for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Matt Citak of the Giants' official site reports. That's not to say Nabers won't be tagged with a designation once the Giants post their final Week 9 injury report Friday, but it appears his absence from Thursday's practice due to a knee issue was merely a blip on the radar. He's strung together four consecutive 100-yard performances, a stretch in which his receiving line sits at 36-509-2 on 51 targets.
